label: late-episode D2 after a rewarded a2->S2 stay, landing in S2 via common transition
explanation: Fires only at D2, only when the agent chose a2 and reached S2 via a common transition, only when the previous trial was rewarded (and the previous choice was also a2, i.e. a stay; the window-first trial with unknown prev_action is allowed), and only near the end of the episode (ep_trial >= ~86; zero activation before trial ~79). All variables are observed at D2 (ep_trial is an implicit clock the GRU tracks; the model value head is low at the same steps, value < 6 gives a similar F1 of 0.84). Never fires at D1/GO, on a1/S1, on rare transitions, or after unrewarded trials. Magnitude grows along streaks of consecutive rewarded a2->S2c trials and with lateness in the episode; misses are the weak low-quartile activations around trials 80-85. False positives are mostly matching steps early in the end window or right after a rare/unrewarded break in the streak.

issues: Systematic false-positive class the predicate leaves out: the previous trial reached its state by a RARE transition. On test, original predicate & (prev_common==0) predicts 1865 steps at precision 0.049 (recall 0.008). That is about 60% of the predicate's ~3100 test false positives. The unit needs the previous trial to be a COMMON rewarded a2->S2 trial, not just any rewarded a2 trial. On dev, prev_common==0 holds only 77 of 11759 activations.

Adding (prev_common != 0) raises test F1 from 0.826 to 0.885 with the ep_trial>=86 clock (P 0.882, R 0.888, mass recall 0.976). With value<6 in place of the clock it reaches 0.905 (P 0.936, R 0.875, mass recall 0.980). So the reported predicate and its numbers understate how specific the unit is.

The label 'after a rewarded a2->S2 stay' overclaims relative to the predicate. The predicate only checks prev_reward==1 and prev_action!=1. It never checks that the previous trial landed in S2, and that condition is exactly where the systematic false positives are.

Minor: 'never fires after unrewarded trials' is not literally true. On dev, 485 of 11759 activations (4.1%) have prev_reward==0, though they carry only 0.6% of the activation mass. They are weak decaying tails right after a streak breaks.

Claims that check out: active only at D2 (0 activations at D1 and GO); 0 when common==0 (the current trial is never rare); essentially 0 when prev_action==1 (10 of 11759); 4 activations in trials 70-79 and none before; reported test scores reproduce (0.767 / 0.896 / 0.826 / 0.979). Firing is also lower when good==1: 822 test predictions at precision 0.685 vs 0.898 when good==2, a secondary modulation.
